candidates.label: Acute ischemic stroke, left medullary infarction (Wallenberg syndrome)
missing_or_uncertain: Underlying cause (e.g., vertebral artery dissection) not confirmed

candidates.label: Acute ischemic stroke, other brainstem location (e.g., pontine)
missing_or_uncertain: Specific brainstem location not supported by MRI

candidates.label: Intracerebral hemorrhage
missing_or_uncertain: No evidence of acute hemorrhage on CT or MRI

candidates.label: Multiple sclerosis (acute demyelinating plaque)
missing_or_uncertain: MRI shows infarction, not demyelination; no typical MS features

candidates.label: Functional neurological disorder (conversion disorder)
missing_or_uncertain: MRI confirms organic lesion; no psychological stressors documented

response.rationale: MRI clearly demonstrates recent ischemic infarction in the left medulla, which explains the crossed neurological findings (right hemiparesis and left ptosis). Other differentials are either contradicted by imaging (hemorrhage, demyelination) or lack supportive evidence (functional disorder). The negative CT is not contradictory as early medullary infarcts are often missed on noncontrast CT.
